title: Host-to-Engram named-root binding event (named_root_bind bound/ended) per Engram host contract v1
outcome: Host-to-Engram named-root binding event (named_root_bind bound/ended) per Engram host contract v1
acceptance: Bind, status and begin responses decode all three named_root states and tolerate absent and unknown states; a refusal, or an uncertain transport or persistence outcome, never reports an unconfirmed root as successfully named and never credits evidence against it.

Checkpoint source sightings carry the capture's matching generation and state and retain workspace identity across rename and clear; tests and acceptance evaluation use the correct named worktree; evidence from a foreign workspace or generation cannot count as a named-root check.

Clear and host cleanup record the matching ended event with the allowed reason, repeating the bound generation's workspace and named_at; rename advances the generation; authoritative named_root reconciliation preserves handoff and recovery bindings and prevents a release and re-claim from reviving an old generation, without inferring release from fence or revision changes.
Focused regression checks exercise the production naming, reconciliation and checkpoint paths for these transitions and failure cases, and pass in a host-recorded check in the item's named root.

Naming a claimed registered worktree records the contract's bound event with the exact source-capture workspace identity, a positive generation, its named_at and a stable retry key derived from (claim_id, generation, kind); retries and restart recovery neither duplicate nor silently lose the transition.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact reviewed tree, its run directory and fingerprint cited in a note.

docs/features/engram-host-adapter.md describes the binding event, the reconciliation from named_root, and the refusal and unknown-outcome handling, cross-linked both ways with any feature brief it references.
